author: First Floor Finance
title: Seems like this happens every time Apple ( AAPL ) is set to
text:
Seems like this happens every time Apple ( AAPL ) is set to release an earnings report, but once again, there are concerns that Apple's sales won't meet expectations when they report earnings next Friday. Apple closed at $171.37, down almost 5% from it's $180.10 peak on January 18th. 
AAPL data by YCharts Over the past few days multiple firms, including JPMorgan and KGI , have expressed concern over demand for the iPhone X. We've seen this story multiple times before, and it's generally led to great trading opportunities. If you go back to September 2016, shares fell about 2% after GfK raised concerns about demand for the iPhone 7 . So what happened next?
Apple jumped more than 6% following the next earnings release after posting record sales and profit numbers. And what about those demand concerns? Well, iPhone 7 and iPhone 7 Plus were the two best-selling cellphones in the world in Q1 2017 . 
Apple has a tremendous track record when it comes to earnings reports. Since 2013, it has met or exceeded its sales forecasts 70% of the time and met or exceeded its profit forecasts 95% of the time. Simply put, it doesn't pay to bet on Apple missing forecasts.
While history is important, you shouldn't invest in something solely off historical patterns, so let's take a quick look at some current numbers.
The research firm Canalys currently estimates that Apple shipped 29 million iPhone Xs in its most recent quarter which ended in December. This is an astounding number, especially when you consider that the iPhone X only accounted for 14.7% of Apple device activations around Christmas time. 

( Source )
Apple's older models of phones are still seeing incredible demand. A recent article by Mark Hibben conservatively estimates that Apple's iPhone sales could top $100 million in the quarter which ended this past December. That would be good for over 27% growth year-over-year. 
This 5% pullback pre-earnings report has created a solid trading opportunity for short-term traders who believe these negative estimates will be proven inaccurate as they have been in the past, but should long-term investors also be looking to get into Apple at these levels?
In my opinion, the answer is a resounding yes.
Don't be scared by Apple's incredible run up over the past year. It's still relatively cheap. It currently trades at a 10.63 EV/EBITDA ratio, which is 25% discount to the S&P 500, which was a forward EV/EBITDA of 14.1. 
AAPL EV to EBITDA (Forward) data by YCharts That's an incredible discount for the company that controls around 30% of the world's smartphone market and 33% of the world's personal computer market. Not to mention, the company has boatloads of cash and a juicy 21% profit margin. Currently, the company could pay off all of its debt and still have over $150 billion in cash left over. 
Also, the company is still growing at a steady pace. Apple's sales and earnings numbers last year were up 6% and 11% respectively year-over-year.
Apple's pre-earnings pullback, which we've seen before, not only creates a great opportunity for traders over the next week, but also allows long-term investors to invest in one of the best companies in the world 5% cheaper than it could only a few days ago.
